newsitem.title: UK: Age can make your brown eyes blue, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Age can make your brown eyes blue, study finds.

text.p: Your eye colour can change throughout your life, making its use as an identifying characteristic questionable, scientists said on Thursday.
Laszlo Bito and colleagues at New York's Columbia University found that 16.6 percent of the 187 pairs of twins they checked showed a change in eye colour bteween the age of six to adulthood.
They tested twins to see if the lightening or darkening of eye colour was genetic or caused by outside factors. "It's not much different than greying of the hair," Bito told New Scientist magazine.
Identical twins, who are genetically alike, tended to change eye colour in the same way. Fraternal twins, who are as closely related as any brother or sister, showed different patterns.
Bito, who reported his findings in the Archives of Ophthalmology, said the shift in eye colour could cause trouble. Eye colour is used to identify holders of U.S. driving licenses, for example.
